facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 the applicant was arrested during the dispersal of a political rally at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow.

The aim of the demonstration was to protest against abuses and falsifications in the course of the elections to the State Duma and of the President of the Russian Federation, and to demand fair elections, respect for human rights, the rule of law and the international obligations of the Russian Federation.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant arrived at Bolotnaya Square at around 6 p.m. to take part in the meeting.
The applicant stood in front of the stage on Bolotnaya Embankment, within the area designated as the meeting venue.
According to the applicant, between 6 p.m. and 7 p.m. the area around him remained peaceful, although there was general confusion.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant was arrested during the dispersal of a political rally at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow.
The applicant was detained at the police station for at least thirty-six hours pending administrative proceedings.
The applicant was sentenced to fifteen days' administrative detention.

The applicant claimed that he had heard the police orders made through a megaphone to disperse, but in the general commotion he was unable to leave immediately and remained within the authorised meeting area until 7 p.m., when he was arbitrarily arrested by the police dispersing the demonstration.
The police apprehended the applicant and took him to a police van, where he waited for an hour before it left Bolotnaya Square for the police station.

The applicant was found guilty of disobeying lawful police orders and was sentenced under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation to fifteen days' administrative detention.

In the administrative proceedings, the applicant was found guilty of failure to obey lawful police orders, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation provided that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of the officer's official duties relating to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the officer's performance of his or her official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between RUB 500 and RUB 1,000 or by administrative detention for up to fifteen days.
According to the Government, the applicant was arrested at 8.30 p.m. at Bolotnaya Square because he was obstructing the traffic and had disregarded the police order to move away.

The rest of Police Officer Y.'s report was a printed template stating that the applicant, acting in a group of citizens, took part in an authorised meeting, went out onto the road and thus obstructed the traffic, did not react to the multiple demands of the police to vacate the road, thereby disobeying a lawful order of the police, who were fulfilling their service duty of maintaining public order and ensuring safety, and thereby committed an administrative offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of the Russian Federation provided that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of the officer's official duties relating to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the officer's performance of his or her official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between RUB 500 and RUB 1,000 or by administrative detention for up to fifteen days.
The applicant stood in front of the stage on Bolotnaya Embankment, within the area designated as the meeting venue.
According to the applicant, between 6 p.m. and 7 p.m. the area around him remained peaceful, although there was general confusion.
The applicant claimed that he had not heard any announcement of the termination of the meeting.

The applicant claimed that he had heard the police orders made through a megaphone to disperse, but in the general commotion he was unable to leave immediately and remained within the authorised meeting area until 7 p.m., when he was arbitrarily arrested by the police dispersing the demonstration.
The applicant denied that he had received any warning or orders before being arrested.
According to the applicant, there was no traffic at Bolotnaya Square at the time of his arrest; it was still suspended.

On the basis of the report written by Police Officer Y., the Justice of the Peace of circuit no. 100 of the Yakimanka district established that at 8.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the applicant had been walking along the road at Bolotnaya Square and obstructing the traffic, and that he had then disobeyed lawful police orders to vacate the venue.
The Justice of the Peace rejected as unreliable two eyewitnesses' testimonies to the effect that the police had not given the applicant any orders or warnings before arresting him.
Ms S. testified that at 9.03 p.m. on 6 May 2012 she had been at Bolotnaya Square; the site had been fully cordoned off and the traffic had not resumed.
Unlike on 4 February 2012, the park at Bolotnaya Square was excluded from the meeting venue on 6 May 2012, which was limited to Bolotnaya Embankment.

A cordon of riot police in full protection gear barred access to the park at Bolotnaya Square and continued along the whole perimeter of the meeting area, channelling the demonstration to Bolotnaya Embankment.
The cordon officers did not enter into any discussion with the protest leaders and no senior officer was delegated to negotiate.

During the period between 5.20 p.m. and 5.45 p.m., no senior police officers or municipal officials came to the site of the sit-down protest, and there was no direct communication between the authorities and the leaders of the sit-in.

The Expert Commission noted that the police did not inform the organisers of the changes they had decided upon, and the organisers only became aware of the police-imposed changes to the event when they arrived at the site on the afternoon of 6 May 2012.

The Expert Commission's report stated that from the moment difficulties first arose for demonstrators attempting to cross Malyy Kamennyy Bridge, demonstrators made repeated attempts to negotiate with the police over moving their cordons to allow protesters onto Bolotnaya Square.

The Expert Commission's report stated that Mr D. Oreshkin, a member of the Presidential Human Rights Council, and State Duma deputy Mr G. Gudkov tried to talk to the police authorities at around 5.30 p.m., but there was no response.

The Expert Commission's report quoted organiser Ms N. Mityushkina as stating that she tried unsuccessfully to find the responsible people in the Ministry of the Interior to solve organisational problems, and that only at 6.00-6.30 p.m. did a senior police officer approach her and tell her that the authorities had suspended the demonstration and ask her to announce from the stage that the event was over.

The Expert Commission's report quoted organiser Mr I. Bakirov as stating that a police officer in a colonel's uniform contacted him only once, and that later when clashes with the police erupted he could not find anyone with whom to communicate and cooperate.

The Expert Commission's report quoted organiser Mr S. Davidis as stating that he personally did not meet nor have time to get into contact with the authorities regarding the fences set up around the perimeter of the rally, and that he only saw OMON officers who behaved aggressively and were not predisposed to get into a conversation.

Mr S. Davidis testified that the closure of the park was not discussed at the working meeting on 4 May 2012, and that it was expressly stated that everything except the position of the stage would be the same as on 4 February 2012.

Ms N. Mirza testified that as she was later told by Police Colonel V. Biryukov, the protesters had sat down on the ground because the passage had been narrowed down, and she confirmed that the passage was much narrower than usual and there were metal detectors which were not supposed to be there.

Mr N. Svanidze testified that he asked why the passage would not be opened, but Police Colonel V. Biryukov kept turning his face away and would not answer, and Mr Svanidze understood that there was no point talking to him as he was not in command.

Mr Vasilyev testified that the Ombudsman told Police Colonel V. Biryukov to let the cordon be moved back so that people could pass, but Police Colonel V. Biryukov told him that it was outside his powers and that he did not know in whose powers it was, at which point the police began breaking the crowd up.

The witness Mr I. Ponomarev testified in the proceedings against Mr S. Udaltsov and Mr Razvozzhayev that the police cordon had been placed differently from the cordon placed for the similar march on 4 February 2012, and that he proposed to Mr S. Udaltsov that the cordon be pushed back so that the police would go back a few steps and widen access to Bolotnaya Square.

The witness Mr G. Gudkov, deputy of the State Duma, testified in the proceedings against Mr S. Udaltsov and Mr Razvozzhayev that at the request of the organisers he had taken part in the negotiations with the police on moving the cordon back and opening up access to the park at Bolotnaya Square, and that he had reached an agreement with the officers of the Moscow Department of the Interior that the cordon would be moved back, but those who had called for a sit-in, including Mr S. Udaltsov, refused to go to the offices of the Moscow Department of the Interior to sign the necessary documents.

The witness Mr D. Gudkov, deputy of the State Duma, testified in the proceedings against Mr S. Udaltsov and Mr Razvozzhayev that together with Mr G. Gudkov he had conducted negotiations with the police and an agreement had been reached that the cordon at Malyy Kamennyy Bridge would be moved back and access to the park would be opened up, but at that point some young men in hoodies among the protesters began pushing citizens onto the cordon, after which the cordon broke, the police began the arrests and mass disorder ensued.

Section 12(1)(iii) of the Public Events Act required the executive body of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation or the municipal authorities, upon receipt of the notification of a public event, to appoint an authorised representative to assist the event organisers in conducting the event in accordance with the law, with the appointment to be formally made by a written decision sent to the event organiser prior to the scheduled date of the event.

Section 13(2) of the Public Events Act required the representative of the executive body of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation or the municipal authorities to be present at the public event, to assist the event organiser in the conduct of the public event, and to ensure, jointly with the organiser and the authorised representative of the Ministry of the Interior, public order and the safety of citizens and compliance with the law during the event.

Section 14(3) of the Public Events Act required the authorised representative of the Ministry of the Interior to facilitate the conduct of the public event and to ensure, jointly with the organiser and the executive body, public order and the safety of citizens and compliance with the law during the public event.
